facts.content: Patient has had watery diarrhea for 3 days, occurring about 5 to 6 times per day.
The diarrhea onset was preceded by vomiting two times, which has now resolved.
facts.source_text: Onset preceded by 2× vomiting; emesis resolved

facts.content: Stools are watery without blood, and there is no abdominal pain, headache, or myalgias.
facts.source_text: Stools watery, no blood; denies abd pain, HA, myalgias

facts.content: Patient feels dehydrated and weak with minimal oral intake and had a brief low-grade fever on the first day.
facts.source_text: Feels dehydrated, weak; minimal PO intake; brief low-grade fever day 1

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a blue short-acting beta-agonist inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer.
Mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and is a software engineer.
Patient has been off work for 3 days and is a nonsmoker.
Patient consumes alcohol socially.
The assessment is acute viral gastroenteritis leading to watery diarrhea and resolved vomiting.
facts.source_text: Acute viral gastroenteritis → watery diarrhea, resolved vomiting

facts.content: Patient is at risk of mild dehydration.
Intermittent asthma is stable.
Patient is advised to take oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte and increase oral fluid intake liberally.
Paracetamol is advised as needed for fever or weakness.
Patient should rest and remain off work for 1 to 2 days, resuming only after 24 to 48 hours diarrhea-free.
facts.source_text: Rest; remain off work 1–2 d, resume only after 24–48 h diarrhea-free

facts.content: Patient should return to clinic if there is no improvement within 7 days or if symptoms worsen.
facts.source_text: RTC if no improvement ≤7 d or worsening symptoms

facts.content: Continue using the blue inhaler as needed for asthma.
facts.source_text: Continue blue inhaler prn for asthma
